title: One number heard on the radio by Dave Dexter
summary: She sang one song unaccompanied, The One I Love Belongs to Somebody Else; Capitol's Dave Dexter heard the broadcast and sent word through Joe Alexander.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: to do one number, because he told me -- I went up and introduced myself to him when I got there, and he says, "Now, I don't know if you'll have a chance to do more than one song," he said, "because the program is so loaded, you know" but I was just so grateful to him, so this is a case of being in the right place at the right time.

Right. So he said, "The program is so loaded I don't know if you'll have a chance to do more than one tune." He said, "But anyway, we'll see. You may get a chance to do it." And I didn't have -- there was nobody there to play with me, to accompany me, you know, so he says, "Can you work by yourself?" And I said, "Yes, I'll have to." So I went on and did my little number. I did, "The One I love Belongs to Somebody Else," you know. So Dave Dexter from Capitol Records was at home with his wife, and she was pregnant with their daughter, and he heard me. You know, it was broadcast.

It was broadcast. So he -- the whole six hours I think was broadcast -- so he heard the show and he contacted me in the next few days through another friend, Joe Alexander, who was also on that label.
